findings.fix: Add short gotcha bullets with their WHY next to the authorization bullets: '--full-auto fails with unexpected argument on codex-cli 0.162.1, so never copy it from older examples' and 'stderr to /dev/null hides the only failure diagnostics'. Keep the detailed text in Run as it is.

findings.evidence: description names codex exec and resume but no intent keywords such as second opinion, GPT or delegating to another agent
findings.fix: Run or resume OpenAI Codex CLI tasks with `codex exec` or `codex exec resume`, choosing the sandbox (read-only analysis, user-authorized workspace edits, network) and reporting model, effort and whether edits occurred. Use when asked to invoke Codex or a GPT coding agent for review, debugging, refactoring, automated edits, a second opinion, or to continue an existing Codex session, even if the user only says 'ask codex' or 'have GPT look at this'. Not for installing the CLI, configuring credentials, conceptual explanations, summarizing prior output without invocation, or other vendors' CLIs.

findings.evidence: Workflow step 2 'Command or skill?' runs from line 15 to line 24. It packs three things into one numbered step: the command-versus-skill decision, the name-collision lookup in three directories, and a 3-option reply template with its own approval rules. The phased flow is harder to follow, and step 2 now holds the most important checkpoint.
findings.fix: Split it into 'Step 2: Command or skill?' (the decision and the existing-scripts fallback) and 'Step 3: Name collision check' (the lookup plus the reply template, kept word for word). Renumber the later steps and the 'run steps 6-7' cross-reference to match. No content is removed.

findings.evidence: '`\$0` is the FIRST positional argument (`\$ARGUMENTS[0]`); `\$1` is the second.' Claude Code changed its placeholder indexing between releases, so this is a version-sensitive fact. Unlike the Frontmatter and Gotchas facts, the Arguments section gives no source URL and no checked date.
findings.fix: Add the source to the bullet: '(Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills, string substitutions section, checked <date>)'. Or tell the agent to confirm the indexing on that page before relying on $0 versus $1.

findings.evidence: The steps are spread across Frame (line 15 'Final check'), Route by goal, Audience and accuracy checks (line 29 'Before drafting...') and Load by deliverable. The skill never gives them as one ordered sequence.
findings.fix: Add a short ordered procedure near the top: 1) list the facts supplied and the unknowns; 2) pick the route by goal; 3) pick the channel; 4) load the matching reference; 5) draft with What-Why-How or the escalation order; 6) run the Final check. Keep the existing text and point each step to its section.

findings.evidence: '"EOD" is ambiguous across time zones; use an explicit date, time, and zone or ask which zone applies.' Unlike the other gotchas, this one does not say what goes wrong.
findings.fix: Add the consequence, for example: 'a Singapore reader's EOD lands before a New York sender's workday starts, so the deadline is missed with nobody at fault.'

findings.evidence: The channel has a clear default ('Default to the lightest channel the recipient reads daily'), but length and register (executive brevity vs peer detail) have none. commands/compose-email.md defaults to 'under 150 words'.
findings.fix: Add one default with an escape hatch, for example: 'Default to under 150 words and one ask for stakeholder or executive updates; go longer only when the facts supplied need it.'

findings.evidence: Several prompts read like notes, not real user messages ('Email non-technical stakeholders: critical payment issue delays release one week to March 15; QA retests Thursday, update Friday.'). 'files' lists the skill's own references ("references/email-templates.md") instead of input files. 'Informative subject' is a vague assertion.

findings.evidence: Most should-trigger queries are short and full of keywords ('Escalate production issue; lead with impact.', 'Project status report with progress, risks, next steps.'). Few test cases where the user describes the need without naming the domain.
findings.fix: Replace 3-4 terse positives with realistic queries that don't name the domain, for example 'my VP keeps asking what the migration means for Q3, here's what eng told me: ...'. Keep the strong near-miss negatives.

findings.evidence: The unknown-fact rule appears three times with different actions: line 15 'mark anything else `Proposed:` or unknown', line 29 'marked as unknown or ask a targeted question', line 39 'say it is unknown ... label any proposed next step or owner "Proposed:"'. findings.fix: Add one decision rule in Audience and accuracy checks: 'Ask a targeted question when the missing fact blocks the message (recipient, the ask itself); otherwise draft with it marked unknown, or as "Proposed:" when you suggest a value.' Point lines 15 and 39 to it.
